name: Stadium World Tour 2026
summary: One Vergence Group rig carried through 42 stadium dates, with the same tuning from the first downbeat in Toronto to the last show in Mexico City.

image.alt: Concert crowd in front of a stage flown with Adamson line arrays

challenge: Open-air stadiums from 35,000 to 70,000 seats, a 4-hour load-in window and weather that changed by the night. The production needed full-range coverage to the upper bowl without a delay ring at every venue.
solution: Main and side hangs of VGt with VGs flown subwoofers in a cardioid arc, E219 ground subs, and XG8 amplification in pre-wired racks. Array Intelligence models for each venue were built before the tour and reused on the day.
result: Consistent coverage within ±3 dB across the floor and bowls, a 90-minute faster load-in than the previous tour, and no system changes between legs.

quote.text: Every night sounded like the night we tuned it. That consistency is what lets you focus on the show.

name: European Festival Season
summary: Six main stages across three countries, run on one shared system design so guest engineers could walk up and mix.

image.alt: Singer on a festival stage with Adamson arrays

challenge: Strict offsite noise limits next to residential areas while still delivering impact to 60,000 people.
solution: Cardioid sub arrays and tight vertical control from Vergence mains, with CS10 delays tuned in Array Intelligence to keep energy on the audience.
result: All six stages stayed within their offsite limits for the full season with no level cuts during headline sets.

quote.text: We hit the dB limits and the crowd still felt the kick drum in their chest.

name: Grand Concert Hall Renovation
summary: A historic hall gained a discreet reinforcement system that supports amplified concerts without changing the room's architecture.

image.alt: Historic theatre interior with a discreet loudspeaker system

challenge: Heritage rules left only two narrow rigging points per side, and the hall had to stay acoustically neutral for orchestral programmes.
solution: Compact IS10 arrays painted to match the proscenium, IS119 subwoofers hidden under the stage lip and CS7p front fills along the stage edge.
result: Even coverage to the second balcony, with the system invisible from most seats.

quote.text: The system disappears. You notice the music, not the loudspeakers.

name: Opera House Auditorium
summary: Natural-sounding reinforcement for spoken word, musicals and opera in a horseshoe auditorium.
challenge: A horseshoe room with deep balconies where the old point-source system left the side boxes with poor intelligibility.
solution: S10 line arrays at left, centre and right with S118 subwoofers, plus CS7 under-balcony fills on delays.
result: Speech intelligibility raised to STI 0.62 or better in every seat, including the side boxes.

name: Multi-Purpose Arena Upgrade
summary: One permanent system for hockey, basketball and touring concerts, switched between modes from a tablet.

image.alt: Arena bowl with a centre-hung loudspeaker system

challenge: A reflective bowl with a centre-hung scoreboard, and events that change from game-night announcements to full concerts.
solution: A ring of CS10 arrays around the scoreboard, CS119 subwoofers and XG8 amplifiers on a Milan network with MS8.2 switches, recalled by preset.
result: Clear announcements to every seat and a system ready for visiting concert productions to tie into.

quote.text: Game night or concert night, it's one button.

name: Outdoor Stadium Speech System
summary: Weather-resistant arrays that cover a 50,000-seat open stadium with clear voice and music.

image.alt: Stadium crowd at an evening event

challenge: Long throw to the top tier, wind, rain and salt air, and a short installation window between seasons.
solution: Distributed IS10 arrays on the roof edge with IS7p fills under the overhangs, all with weatherised finishes.
result: Installed in eight weeks, with intelligible announcements in every section even in high wind.

name: Contemporary Church Sanctuary
summary: A worship space that needed both concert impact for the band and clear speech for the message.

image.alt: Worship stage with lighting and haze

challenge: A wide fan-shaped room with a low ceiling, volunteer operators and services that move from spoken word to full band in minutes.
solution: A left-centre-right CS10 system with CS119 subwoofers in a cardioid arc, CS7 outfills and simple presets for volunteer engineers.
result: Even coverage across the fan, less low end on stage for the band and a system volunteers can run with confidence.

quote.text: Our volunteers mix with confidence now. The system does the hard part.

name: Cathedral Speech Reinforcement
summary: Steered column arrays bring clear speech to a highly reverberant cathedral nave.

image.alt: Loudspeakers installed in a large interior

challenge: A six-second reverberation time and listed stonework where nothing could be drilled.
solution: IS7 and IS5c arrays on free-standing bases along the nave, aimed precisely at the congregation and away from stone surfaces.
result: Speech is understood throughout the nave for the first time, with no visible change to the building.
